BUS.G12.T2.QUALITY.A1.title: Quality of performance & TQM
BUS.G12.T2.QUALITY.A1.description: How the quality of performance within the business functions influences the success or failure of a business: the concept of quality, its relation to the various functions, and the elements of Total Quality Management (TQM) — continuous skills development, total client satisfaction and continuous improvement of processes and systems.
BUS.G12.T2.QUALITY.A1.strand: T2 — CSR, human rights, teams, sector & environment, leadership & quality
BUS.G12.T2.QUALITY.A1.recovery_strategy: TQM means everyone in every function continuously improves quality: total client satisfaction, ongoing skills development and constant improvement of processes and systems. Poor quality in any function can sink the business.

questions.question: What does 'quality' mean in business?
options: Meeting or exceeding the standards customers expect
Producing as much as possible regardless of standards
questions.expected: Meeting or exceeding the standards customers expect
questions.memo: Quality is about meeting or exceeding the standards and expectations of customers.

questions.question: TQM stands for Total _________ Management.
questions.memo: TQM is Total Quality Management — a whole-business approach to continuously improving quality.

questions.question: True or false: Quality applies to every business function, not just production.
questions.memo: Quality matters in every function — finance, HR, marketing, admin — not only in making the product.

questions.question: Which of these is an element of Total Quality Management?
questions.memo: Continuous improvement of processes and systems is a core element of TQM.

questions.question: Total client _________ is one of the elements of TQM.
questions.memo: Total client satisfaction — fully meeting customers' needs — is a key element of TQM.

questions.question: True or false: Poor quality can contribute to the failure of a business.
questions.memo: Poor quality drives away customers, raises costs through returns and damages reputation, which can lead to failure.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it is a TQM element or not.

items.text: Continuous improvement of processes and systems
Doing a task right once and never reviewing it

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: TQM elements include continuous skills development, total client satisfaction and continuous improvement. Ignoring complaints or cutting quality are not.

questions.question: How does high quality of performance support business success?
options: It satisfies customers, reduces returns and builds a strong reputation
It guarantees the business pays no tax
It removes the need for any customers
questions.expected: It satisfies customers, reduces returns and builds a strong reputation
questions.memo: Good quality keeps customers happy, cuts the cost of returns and rework, and builds the reputation that drives future sales.

questions.question: Thesis: 'Quality must be managed across all business functions, not just production.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: Quality must be managed across all business functions, not just production.

pool.text: Poor quality in finance, admin or service also loses customers and money
Customers judge the whole experience, not only the product
Weakness in one function can drag down the whole business
Only the production line ever affects customers
Quality posters look nice on the wall
Quality is a one-time task that never needs reviewing

questions.memo: The strong reasons are that poor quality anywhere loses money, customers judge the whole experience, and one weak function harms the whole. The others are false or irrelevant.

questions.question: Continuous _________ development keeps staff skilled and is part of TQM.
questions.memo: Continuous skills development keeps the workforce capable of delivering and improving quality — a TQM element.

questions.question: What does quality look like in the finance function?
questions.memo: Quality in finance means accurate, reliable records and reporting — errors here harm the whole business.

questions.question: True or false: TQM is a once-off project that is finished and then forgotten.
questions.memo: TQM is ongoing — it is about continuous improvement, not a single completed task.

questions.question: Sort each example of quality under the business function it belongs to.
questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Defect-free, consistent goods = production quality; accurate, timely records and payments = finance quality; skilled staff and fair recruitment = HR quality.

questions.question: What is a likely impact of consistently poor quality?
options: Returns, lost customers and higher costs
questions.expected: Returns, lost customers and higher costs
questions.memo: Poor quality causes returns, drives customers away and raises costs through rework — the opposite of what a business needs.

questions.question: How does the need for quality differ between a sole trader and a large business?
options: Both need quality, but a large business needs formal systems to maintain it across many staff
Neither needs to worry about quality
questions.expected: Both need quality, but a large business needs formal systems to maintain it across many staff
questions.memo: Every business needs quality; a large business relies on formal quality systems to keep standards consistent across many people and sites.

questions.question: Continuous _________ of processes and systems is a key TQM element.
questions.memo: TQM relies on continuously improving processes and systems so quality keeps rising over time.

questions.question: A well-made product is ruined by slow, rude service and billing errors. How does this affect the business?
options: Quality failures in service and finance can still drive customers away despite the good product
Nothing changes, because the product is good
questions.expected: Quality failures in service and finance can still drive customers away despite the good product
questions.memo: Because customers judge the whole experience, poor service and billing can lose them even when the product itself is excellent.

questions.question: A manager wants to cut quality checks to save money. How should this be evaluated?
options: Risky — short-term savings can be outweighed by returns, lost customers and reputational damage
Always a good idea with no downside
questions.expected: Risky — short-term savings can be outweighed by returns, lost customers and reputational damage
questions.memo: Cutting quality control may save a little now but often costs far more later through defects, returns and lost trust.

questions.question: Why does TQM treat quality as everyone's responsibility?
options: Because quality depends on every function and person, so all must continuously improve
Because quality is fixed and cannot change
Because customers do not notice quality
questions.expected: Because quality depends on every function and person, so all must continuously improve
questions.memo: TQM recognises that quality is created across every function, so it makes continuous improvement everyone's job.

questions.question: How does consistent quality of performance influence whether a business succeeds or fails?
options: High quality builds loyalty and reputation that drive success; poor quality erodes them towards failure
Quality has no link to success or failure
questions.expected: High quality builds loyalty and reputation that drive success; poor quality erodes them towards failure
questions.memo: Quality is a major driver of success: it builds the loyalty and reputation a business depends on, while poor quality steadily undermines them.
